prompt.context_jp: 白石家の食卓には、湯気の消えかけたオムライスの皿___置かれていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 白石家の食卓には、湯気の消えかけたオムライスの皿___置かれていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that introduces the plate as a newly described item on the table.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence opens the scene by introducing a new object the camera lands on — the plate itself is fresh information, so が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the plate as an already-known topic, which clashes with this scene-setting opener. を doesn't fit with 置かれていた (passive, no direct object).

contrast_examples.en: There's a book on the desk. (newly noticed)

contrast_examples.jp: その本は机に置いてある。
contrast_examples.en: That book (we know) is on the desk.

prompt.context_jp: 友利のグラスの中で氷___ゆっくりと崩れ、店内の低い喧騒に呑まれていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 友利のグラスの中で氷___ゆっくりと崩れ…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the ice as a noticed, momentary event?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator notices the ice shifting as a small sensory event — pure description with が. は would turn ice into a topic being compared or discussed.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply 'as for the ice…' setting it against something else, which is not what the quiet mood here does.

prompt.context_jp: 隣のベッドでは他の患者の身動きする気配だけ___して、そのほかの物音は絶えていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: …他の患者の身動きする気配だけ___して…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle follows 〜だけ to say 'only that, nothing else'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけが with a sensory verb like する exhaustively picks out the sole thing audible/present. The contrast with そのほかの物音は絶えていた confirms it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜だけは would stress 'at least that one' as a topic — a different nuance. に doesn't fit as subject marker here.

contrast_examples.en: Only the wind could be heard.
At least this, I won't give up.

prompt.context_jp: 病室の空気は張り詰め、時計の秒針の音だけ___かろうじて存在を主張していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: …時計の秒針の音だけ___かろうじて存在を主張していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle expresses that only the clock's ticking stood out?

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけが highlights the clock-tick as the single thing asserting its presence in the silence — exhaustive 'and nothing else'. が is the natural subject marker here.
feedback.incorrect_en: は with だけ would shift to a contrastive topic ('at least this one'), weakening the vivid 'only X' feel.

contrast_examples.en: He at least stayed behind (others didn't).

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣___寝起きの目で廊下に出て、その後ろ姿に足を止めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 麻衣___寝起きの目で廊下に出て、その後ろ姿に足を止めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces Mai as the continuing topic of the scene?

feedback.correct_en: Mai has already been established as the character in focus; the sentence tells us what she (the topic) does next. は carries the ongoing narrative frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would newly identify Mai as if someone unexpected entered — but she's already the subject of the chapter's attention.

contrast_examples.en: Mai (as topic) stepped into the hall.
It was Mai who stepped into the hall.

prompt.context_jp: 圭介___箸に手を伸ばしながらも、娘の横顔からしばらく目を離さなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 圭介___箸に手を伸ばしながらも、娘の横顔からしばらく目を離さなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Keisuke as the already-known topic of the sentence?

feedback.correct_en: Keisuke is the central character we've been following. は simply resumes him as topic for a new comment about his behavior.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would single him out as new or contrastive information, which doesn't match this calm continuation.

contrast_examples.en: It was Keisuke who fell silent.

prompt.context_jp: 「いつも いつも やりすぎなのよ あなた___」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「いつも いつも やりすぎなのよ あなた___」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle makes 'you' a contrastive/pointed topic (unlike others)?

feedback.correct_en: Marika is calling Keisuke out — 'you (as opposed to normal people) always overdo it.' Postposed あなたは is contrastive, scolding topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: あなたが would sound like identifying who did it (new info); it loses the exasperated 'you, of all people' tone.

contrast_examples.en: You go too far (that's just like you).
It was you who did it.

prompt.context_jp: 「ええ うちの守屋___頑張りまして」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ええ うちの守屋___頑張りまして」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle presents Moriya as 'the one who' did the work?

feedback.correct_en: The speaker proudly singles out Moriya as the one responsible — exhaustive/identifying が. It answers an implicit 'who put this together?'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would downgrade it to 'as for Moriya, she worked hard,' losing the modest-boast of pointing her out as THE person behind it.

contrast_examples.jp: うちの娘が作ったんです。
contrast_examples.en: My daughter is the one who made it.

contrast_examples.jp: うちの娘は料理が上手。
contrast_examples.en: My daughter (as topic) is a good cook.

prompt.context_jp: 「あれは シェフ___よかったんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あれは シェフ___よかったんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle credits the chef as the specific reason it worked?

feedback.correct_en: Keisuke deflects praise: 'It was the CHEF who was good' — identifying/exhaustive が picks out the credit-receiver.
feedback.incorrect_en: シェフは would make the chef a topic being described, losing the 'it's thanks to the chef' pinpointing nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 「3日前のLINE___ いつまでニヤニヤ見てんのよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「3日前のLINE___ いつまでニヤニヤ見てんのよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the LINE message as the thing being looked at?

feedback.correct_en: 見る takes a direct object — the LINE is what she's staring at, so を is the natural marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: が/は would reframe LINE as a subject or topic, breaking the teasing 'you're staring at…' structure.

prompt.context_jp: 「麻衣___ 恋してるみたいね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「麻衣___ 恋してるみたいね」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here — Marika sharing a tender observation about Mai?

feedback.correct_en: She's commenting ON Mai (already known to both). 'As for Mai — she seems to be in love.' Topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 麻衣が would sound like identifying who's in love in response to a question — too abrupt for this gentle disclosure.

prompt.context_jp: 「麻衣も いつまでも 10歳の子供じゃないし 時___流れるのよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「…時___流れるのよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits a general truth: 'time flows'?

feedback.correct_en: Generic/aphoristic statements use は — 'time (as a general topic) flows.' It frames a truth, not a one-time event.
feedback.incorrect_en: 時が流れる can appear in narration of a specific moment, but here Marika is stating a maxim, so は is natural.

prompt.context_jp: 「私は かまわなかったのよ あなた___誰かと 一緒になってくれていても」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「…あなた___誰かと 一緒になってくれていても」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside this subordinate clause for 'you'?

feedback.correct_en: In subordinate clauses like 〜ても with a new predicate, the embedded subject is marked by が. 私は sits as the main topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: あなたは would create two competing topics in one sentence and sound awkward here — は tends to stay in the main clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 私は彼が来ても気にしない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't mind even if he comes.

contrast_examples.jp: 私は彼は来ないと思う。

prompt.context_jp: 部長の顔色___普段と違うことは、離れた席からも一目で分かった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部長の顔色___普段と違うことは…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks '顔色' inside the こと-clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a nominalized こと-clause, the embedded subject takes が. The outer topic marker は attaches to こと.
feedback.incorrect_en: 顔色は would make 'the boss's complexion' the overarching topic, conflicting with 〜ことは further out.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来ることは知っていた。
contrast_examples.en: I knew that he was coming.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は来ることを知っていた。

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外では夕方の光___徐々に赤みを帯び始めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓の外では夕方の光___徐々に赤みを帯び始めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for scenic description of the light turning red?

feedback.correct_en: Pure scene description — the light is observed as a new, unfolding phenomenon, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 光は would single out light as a topic of discussion, out of place in this cinematic beat.

prompt.context_jp: 「ええっ 守屋さんでも そんなことあるんだ？ 君___ 長女でしょ？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「…君___ 長女でしょ？」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this teasing 'you're the eldest, right?' line?

feedback.correct_en: 'As for you — you're the eldest, right?' Nakamura is identifying Moriya's role as a known attribute. Topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 君が長女 would answer 'who is the eldest?' — an identifying flavor that doesn't match this casual observation.

prompt.context_jp: 台所の湯気___薄れ、朝食の支度は思いのほか静かに整えられていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 台所の湯気___薄れ、朝食の支度は思いのほか静かに整えられていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the steam as a quietly observed change?

feedback.correct_en: Narrative description — the steam thinning is a new sensory observation, so が. Compare the explicit topic 朝食の支度は in the same sentence.
feedback.incorrect_en: 湯気は would make steam a topic contrasted with something, overloading the sentence with two topics.

prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adverb Rion uses to tell Mai to 'just hurry up and ask' her crush.

feedback.correct_en: とっとと is casual/blunt 'hurry up already' — perfectly fits Rion needling Mai to just ask him.
feedback.incorrect_en: そろそろ ('about time now') is too mild and polite for this push. のろのろ ('slowly, sluggishly') is the opposite of what she wants.

contrast_examples.en: It's about time to head home.

prompt.context_jp: 「知らないおっさんに 朝から______されて お母さん呼ばわりされたら 余計 不安になるわよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「知らないおっさんに 朝から______されて…」
prompt.prompt_en: What verb captures Keisuke's unexpected morning intrusion?

feedback.correct_en: 突撃される 'to get rushed at / stormed in on' matches Marika's exasperated tone about Keisuke barging in uninvited.
feedback.incorrect_en: 訪問される is too neutral/polite for this scolding. 案内される ('to be guided') makes no sense here.

contrast_examples.en: I got barged in on first thing in the morning.
I received a (proper) visit in the morning.

prompt.context_jp: 「仕事で ヘコんでるときとか 新島さんと話してると なんか… 味方でいてくれる気がして ______」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「…味方でいてくれる気がして ______」
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression means 'I feel relieved'?

feedback.correct_en: ホッとする captures the 'take a load off, feel safe' relief Moriya describes when talking to Niijima.
feedback.incorrect_en: ドキドキする ('heart-pounding') suggests excitement/nerves. イライラする ('irritated') is the opposite feeling.

contrast_examples.jp: 話を聞いてホッとした。
contrast_examples.en: I felt relieved after hearing it.

contrast_examples.jp: 試合前にドキドキする。
contrast_examples.en: My heart's pounding before the match.

prompt.context_jp: 「______頑張りましょう いいレシピも集まってきてますし」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「______頑張りましょう」
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase means 'don't get discouraged'?

feedback.correct_en: 気落ちする = to feel let down / disheartened. Niijima is telling Moriya not to get crushed by the setback.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気を失う means 'to lose consciousness' — too literal. 気がつく ('to notice') doesn't fit a pep-talk.

contrast_examples.jp: 失敗しても気落ちしないで。
contrast_examples.en: Don't be discouraged even if you fail.

prompt.context_jp: 「そういうのは 君の______じゃない 小学生に頼ってんじゃないわよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「そういうのは 君の______じゃない」
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'your specialty / forte'?

feedback.correct_en: 十八番 (おはこ/じゅうはちばん) is the set expression for 'one's signature skill / forte' — Marika teases that organizing is Keisuke's thing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一番 just means 'first/best in rank', not a signature skill. 番外 means 'extra, outside the lineup' — opposite meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: この曲は彼の十八番だ。
contrast_examples.en: This song is his signature piece.

prompt.context_jp: 「それなら きっと なくなってはないよ まあ ______されて 今までとは 別の場所に保存されてるとか そういう状態なのかも」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「まあ ______されて 今までとは 別の場所に保存されてる…」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb matches Keisuke's computer-memory metaphor (data being 'compressed')?

feedback.correct_en: 圧縮 ('compressed') fits his analogy with computer storage — the memories are tucked away, not gone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 消去 means 'erased' — contradicts his reassurance. 分解 ('taken apart') breaks the data metaphor.

prompt.context_jp: 「まあ そんな白石も ______なくて好きだったけど」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「…そんな白石も ______なくて好きだったけど」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb form means 'couldn't leave her alone'?

feedback.correct_en: 放っておく → 放っとく → 放っとけない = 'can't just leave (someone) alone,' a classic warm-feelings expression.
feedback.incorrect_en: 置いとけない (literally 'can't put aside') isn't idiomatic for feelings. 忘れとけ isn't a standard form here.

contrast_examples.jp: あの子は放っとけない。
contrast_examples.en: I can't just leave that kid alone.

prompt.prompt_jp: 「______ね～」(a coworker gossiping about Moriya's slip-up)
prompt.prompt_en: Which casual expression means 'she really screwed up'?

feedback.correct_en: やらかす is slangy for 'to mess up / do something careless.' Fits the gossipy, slightly cruel tone of the coworker.
feedback.incorrect_en: やりきる means 'see through to the end' (positive). やりなおす means 'redo' — neither captures 'blundered'.

contrast_examples.jp: また やらかしたね。

contrast_examples.en: I pushed it through to the end.

prompt.context_jp: Marika politely asks Keisuke to stop calling her mother. Which phrasing feels most natural for the scene?
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Marika's exasperated-but-polite request to drop 'お母さん'?

choices.text: その“お母さん”っていうのだけ やめてもらえます？
その“お母さん”というものだけ 中止してくれますか？
あの“お母さん”なるものを 禁止していただけますか？

feedback.correct_en: The chapter uses 〜のだけやめてもらえます？ — a soft, conversational request that still keeps distance. Natural for a child-adult hybrid trying to be polite without being stiff.
feedback.incorrect_en: 中止する/禁止する sound like official procedures. ものだけ / なるもの are over-formal and unidiomatic for daily speech.

contrast_examples.jp: それ、やめてもらえます？

prompt.context_jp: After Moriya apologizes in the office, which reply from Keisuke sounds most natural?
prompt.prompt_en: Which response fits a senior colleague gently taking the blame?

choices.text: 異動してきたばっかりの守屋さんに 任しちゃったのは 俺だし ちょっと早かった ってことなんだな
異動してきたばっかりの守屋さんを 任命してしまいましたので 時期尚早でございました
守屋さん 異動したて 任せた 俺 悪い 早すぎた

feedback.correct_en: Option a mirrors Keisuke's warm senior-to-junior speech: casual connectives (〜しちゃった, 〜だし) with reflective ってことなんだな. Natural in-office kindness.
feedback.incorrect_en: b sounds like a formal apology letter — too stiff. c is choppy telegraphese that would feel cold or robotic.

prompt.context_jp: A ten-year-old delivers an elaborate invitation. Which version matches the comic tone (over-polite from a child)?
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing feels most like Marika's overly-formal invitation?

choices.text: 突然のおうかがい 失礼いたします。今度の日曜日 バーベキューがあるのですが…
いきなり来てごめんね。日曜日 バーベキューやるんだけど…
急にすみません、日曜バーベキューするよ。

feedback.correct_en: The joke rests on an elementary schooler using business-grade keigo. a mirrors that mismatch: 突然のおうかがい失礼いたします… is textbook adult etiquette.
feedback.incorrect_en: b and c are age-appropriate casual speech — natural for a kid, but they lose the humor of 'over-polite grown-up voice in a child's body.'

contrast_examples.jp: 突然のご連絡失礼いたします。

prompt.context_jp: Keisuke echoes Marika's 'time flows.' Which reply sounds most natural as a reflective echo?
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the most natural wistful echo of her 'time flies' line.

feedback.correct_en: He echoes her generic aphorism verbatim with は — reflecting on the general truth, not a specific stretch of time.
feedback.incorrect_en: 時が流れる would sound like describing a specific event, not pondering a maxim. 時を流れる is ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.en: Time flows — that's just how it is.

prompt.context_jp: Keisuke clowns at accepting the barbecue-organizer role as if receiving a formal appointment. Which version matches the chapter's exaggerated keigo bit?
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the version that fits his mock-formal 'accepting an appointment' joke.

choices.text: 喜んで幹事やらせていただきます

feedback.correct_en: The humor comes from laying on 喜んで〜させていただきます (polite business reception language) at home. a captures that satirical formality.
feedback.incorrect_en: b is just casual acceptance — no joke. c sounds boastful/combative, wrong for the mood of begging-not-to-be-abandoned.

contrast_examples.jp: やらせていただきます。
